text: Quiet Luxury is the defining menswear aesthetic of 2024–2025. The look centers on understated, impeccably fitted pieces: cashmere crewnecks, tailored trousers in camel or grey flannel, and clean leather loafers. Brands like The Row, Loro Piana, and Brunello Cucinelli lead the category. Avoid logos. Let quality of fabric and cut do the talking. Works best on oval and oblong face shapes with a defined jawline.

Coastal Grandfather — the relaxed, sun-bleached take on preppy dressing. Key pieces: wide-brimmed linen hats, oversized linen blazers in ecru or sky blue, canvas sneakers, and relaxed chino shorts. This trend flatters medium and olive skin tones most, and pairs well with wavy or straight hair. Heart and oval face shapes carry the relaxed silhouette best.

Dark Academia revival continues into 2025 — think tweed blazers, turtleneck knits, Oxford-cap-toe shoes, and heavy wool coats. The palette is deep: chocolate brown, hunter green, burgundy, and charcoal. Deep and tan skin tones make these colors absolutely pop. Square and diamond face shapes particularly suit the structured collars and lapels.

Gorpcore has moved from trail to street. Technical fabrics, utility vests with multiple pockets, trail runners (Salomon XT-6, Hoka Clifton), and weather-proof anorak jackets define the trend. Brands: Arc'teryx, Patagonia, and The North Face Purple Label. Particularly strong for round and oblong face shapes who benefit from the structured volume of technical outerwear.

Dopamine Dressing — bold, joy-forward color blocking using saturated hues. Electric blue paired with tangerine, lime green with cobalt, or head-to-toe cherry red. Statement accessories: chunky resin jewelry, color-coordinated bags. Works brilliantly on fair and deep skin tones where contrast is maximized. Oval face shapes have the freedom to experiment most with bold accessories.

Y2K Streetwear nostalgia is in full swing: low-rise jeans (Diesel), graphic baby tees, track suits in velour or nylon, and chunky dad sneakers (New Balance 990, ASICS Gel-Kayano 14). Platform shoes add height and work well for round face shapes to create elongation. Olive and medium skin tones look especially good in the warm browns and pop colors characteristic of early-2000s palettes.

Workwear Chic: power dressing has returned with an elevated, modern spin. Oversized double-breasted blazers in pinstripe, wide-leg wool trousers, pointed-toe mules, and silk blouses. The silhouette creates a strong shoulder line that balances a heart or round face. Light and fair skin tones shine in the classic navy × ivory workwear palette.

Vintage Denim Revival: raw-selvedge and distressed denim in every cut — straight leg, flare, and carpenter. Paired with vintage band tees, trucker jackets, and retro white sneakers (Converse, New Balance 574). This look works across all face shapes and is particularly flattering on wavy and curly hair textures worn naturally. Olive and tan skin tones glow in indigo denim.

The Linen Suit Moment: unstructured linen suits in natural, sage, or chalk are the defining warm-weather formalwear of 2025. Wear single-breasted, one-button with a plain white tee or a relaxed collarless shirt. Especially elegant on medium-to-olive skin tones. The relaxed structure softens a square jaw and adds sophistication to an oblong face.

Monochrome Dressing: head-to-toe single-color outfits create a long, lean line. Popular tones: all-black (evergreen), all-camel, all-white, all-terracotta. The elongating effect benefits round and oblong face shapes by drawing the eye vertically. Deep and fair skin tones create the most striking visual impact in high-contrast monochromes like all-white or all-black.

Barrel-Leg and Wide-Leg Denim is the trouser silhouette of the moment. High-waisted with a generous thigh and a taper at the ankle, creating an hourglass or triangular silhouette from the waist down. Works as a counterbalance for heart and diamond face shapes — wider jaw line needs width at the hips to create balance. Best in raw indigo or washed-stone tones.

Statement Outerwear as the hero piece: the single investment item that defines an entire look. Think sculptural wool coats (A.P.C., Max Mara), oversized puffers in camel or cobalt, or sherpa-lined trucker jackets. For square and heart face shapes, structured coats with strong lapels add dramatic framing. Fair and light skin tones pop inside camel and ivory outerwear.

Elevated Basics: the capsule wardrobe philosophy is trending. High-quality versions of simple pieces: heavyweight plain tees (230 g/m²), classic Breton stripe tops, perfectly fitted chinos, and clean white leather sneakers. Brands excelling here: Uniqlo U, Arket, and COS. This understated look works on every face shape — the focus is on fit and fabric.

Sheer and Lightweight Layering: mesh tops, organza blouses, and sheer knit cardigans worn over minimal underlayers. The lightness of these pieces creates dimension without bulk. Perfect for oval and heart face shapes where softness in the upper body complements the face. Tan and olive skin tones look stunning in warm-nude sheers.

Relaxed Tailoring for men: the oversized blazer worn with wide-leg trousers and chunky loafers. The proportions are deliberately large — a true departure from the slim-fit era. This trend suits oblong faces particularly well, as the wide shoulders create horizontal interest. Light skin tones suit the trend's neutral palette of sand, stone, and slate.

Maximalist Jewelry: bold, sculptural pieces as the focal point of an otherwise minimal outfit. Chunky gold chain necklaces, oversized hoop earrings, stacked bangles in brass or resin. These pieces draw attention to the jawline and neck, working especially well for those with defined or sharp jaw types. Deep and tan skin tones glow in gold tones.

Ballet-Core Dressing: satin slip skirts, ballet flats, wrap cardigans, and soft pink / blush / powder blue palettes. Delicate and feminine, this look works beautifully with straight and wavy hair. Fair and light skin tones shine in the pastel palette. Upturned and almond eye shapes are particularly complemented by the softness of this aesthetic.

The Leather Jacket Renaissance: from biker to moto to oversized and cropped, leather outerwear is evergreen in 2025. Black leather biker jackets: timeless for square and diamond face shapes. Tan/caramel leather works for olive and medium skin tones. Cropped leather bombers flatter those with longer faces (oblong) by creating a horizontal break at the waist.

Tonal Earthtones: building outfits within the warm neutral spectrum — terracotta, burnt sienna, caramel, dusty rose, and warm white. This palette is the 2025 alternative to all-beige and feels more dimensional. It is particularly flattering on olive, tan, and deep skin tones. Works well with coily and curly hair textures, celebrating natural volume.

Capsule Sneaker Rotation: instead of one statement sneaker, the trend is three complementary pairs covering every occasion. White low-top (Nike Air Force 1), clean runner (New Balance 990v6), and a fashion sneaker (Adidas Gazelle or Samba). Sneaker styling works across all face shapes, allowing the upper body and facial features to take center stage — a great entry point for any style journey.
